title: Elio's Special Stand
markdown:
Elio the fox loved to make things. His fur was the warm colour of autumn leaves, and his long tail swayed gently when his clever mind was busy, which was almost always. School was getting ready for Presentation Day, when woodland creatures shared something they had learned or made. Elio wanted his sharing to be just right, so he imagined a tiny platform, no taller than a fat mushroom. A quiet, steady place to stand and share his thoughts in a soft, clear voice.

He told his dear friend Pearl, a little sparrow with feathers that sparkled like morning dew. Pearl chirped, tiny head bobbing. "Oh, Elio, that sounds lovely! A special spot for you to feel just right!"

Together they found smooth pale wood from an old oak, and tiny nails that shone like little stars. Elio worked with deep quiet focus, brow furrowed in sweet thought. Pearl brought soft moss to make the platform cozy, or a juicy berry for a snack. The platform was perfect: smooth, perfectly level. When Elio stepped onto it, he felt calm and ready.

Presentation Day arrived with soft sunshine and a breeze whispering through the leaves. Their classroom nestled inside the strong roots of an old willow, filled with a low happy hum. Elio watched quietly as younger friends — little dormice, shy rabbits — stood on small, sometimes wobbly stools or boxes. Then he noticed something interesting. When those little ones stood on their tiny platforms, they seemed to grow a little taller. Voices became louder. Movements grand, like little actors on a stage. One small rabbit, usually very quiet, stood on his box and spoke with a happy voice about a ladybug. He moved his paws gently as he said it flew, like a tiny jewel in the air. Elio watched, a little surprised, mostly curious. His own small platform made him just a little taller, like a secret window opening a tiny crack.

When it was Elio's turn, he walked calmly to his platform. He didn't feel the need to move grandly. His own gentle wonder was enough. He spoke softly about how dew drops formed on spiderwebs in the early morning light. Each tiny drop was like a little mirror, showing the big blue sky. He shared his quiet observations with a steady voice from his gentle height. The other children listened — some with wide wondering eyes, others with soft kind smiles. Pearl chirped from a nearby branch, a warm flutter of quiet pride. Dr. Hatch, the wise old owl who led their school, blinked his large kind eyes and gave a slow approving hoot.

Elio finished. A calm feeling, like a warm tide, washed over him. He stepped down, perfectly content. The little extra height was interesting, a fun observation. He knew the best way to share was still his quiet thoughtfulness. The platform was sturdy and well-made, just like the things he loved to build. His way of sharing was just right for him.

As the sun dipped and long sleepy shadows crossed the meadow, Elio felt a warm tiredness. He thought of his burrow, earthy dried leaves, the quiet promise of morning. He wondered whether next Presentation Day someone else might want a mushroom-high stand too — not to be louder, only to see the dew from a little nearer the sky.

Pearl tucked her head under a wing. Dr. Hatch's hoot followed them home, slow as dusk.
